test-fixtures/analysis/trackmodel-v2.fix.content: Coverage status contradicts the embedded native data. `analysisCoverage2.inputs` marks `native.rekordbox.cues` (and `native.rekordbox.waveforms`) as `absent`, yet `nativeAnalysis.rekordbox` contains a cue entry and `waveformFlags.hasWaveform` is `true`. A parity/readiness fixture whose input flags disagree with the data it carries can let tests pass while the coverage/readiness flags are wrong. Reconcile the input statuses with the embedded native data (e.g. mark both `present`, or drop the corresponding native data).

This gridWarning cannot be produced by the current producer and encodes inconsistent coordinates. In `analysis/src/autolight_analysis/metrical.py` `metrical_vote`:
- `evidence` is emitted as `f"{name}:offset-median-{median}ms"` / `f"{name}:p95-{p95}ms"` (e.g. `beat-this:offset-median-60ms`), not the bare `beat-this:offset` used here.
- `beatRange` is set to `[1, len(native_times)]`, i.e. `[1,4]`; but the grid's beats are 0-indexed (`index` 0–3), so `[1,4]` exceeds the valid max index 3 (off-by-one coordinate mismatch).
- `compare_grids` short-circuits to no warning when `n < minAnchors` (default 32), so a 4-beat grid cannot yield any warning under default config.
The fixture therefore validates a warning shape/range the pipeline never emits; align the evidence string, `beatRange` coordinate base, and anchor count with the producer (or with an explicitly lowered `minAnchors`).

apps/desktop/electron/services/secrets-s.content: This plaintext-persistence assertion is effectively vacuous. `SecretVault.flush()` writes `toBase64(crypto.encryptString(...))`, and `PLAIN` contains `-`, which cannot appear in the base64 alphabet, so `bytes.includes(PLAIN)` can never be true regardless of whether encryption actually happened. Combined with the transparent fake cipher (`encryptString` returns `enc(<plaintext>)`, so the "encrypted" bytes still contain the secret verbatim), the test would still pass even if encryption were removed and the vault wrote `toBase64(JSON.stringify(persist))` directly. Make the fake cipher opaque (e.g. XOR each byte with a fixed key) and assert against the base64-decoded blob so the check genuinely detects a missing/identity encryption step.

Test name promises the cloud key is retained ("keeps the cloud key"), but the body only sets/checks the memory-only agent token — the cloud key is never set and never asserted. The test can pass regardless of a cloud-key persistence regression, so the stated guarantee is unverified. Set `govee.cloud.apiKey` before the restart and assert it is still retrievable (in addition to the agent token being gone), or rename the test to match what it actually verifies.

apps/desktop/electron/services/secrets-s.content: Removal durability is never verified across a restart. The test checks only the in-memory `getSecret` after `removeSecret`, then stops. `removeSecret` ultimately calls `flush()`, which for an empty persistent set writes `clearBlob()` ("blob": null). If `clearBlob` were a no-op (or wrongly rewrote the old blob), the value would remain in the on-disk file and a subsequent start would resurrect it — yet this test would still pass. Add a third `started(file)` cycle and assert `getSecret("govee.cloud.apiKey")` is missing after restart.

The test is titled "redacts every live value at log boundaries" but only the persisted cloud key (`PLAIN`) is set before calling `redactSecrets`/`liveValues()`. The memory-only agent token is a live value too (`liveValues()` returns both ids), yet it is never exercised, so a leak of in-memory secrets through redaction would go undetected. Also set `agent.apiToken` and assert its value is redacted from the same line.

apps/desktop/electron/services/simulator.content: Data integrity: every one of the ~328 beats in this seed grid carries `beatInBar: 1`, so the meter never cycles 1–4. This is not inert: `packages/show-runtime/src/index.ts` derives downbeats with `model.beatGrid.beats.filter((b) => b.beatInBar === 1)` (see its comment `Native downbeats (beatInBar === 1)`). Fed through the real planner/runtime that this seed drives, every beat — including beat indices that should be bar boundaries — will be classified as a native downbeat, so bar-aligned rendering and section-boundary logic in the simulator loop will be exercised against a corrupt grid. Either the fixture is wrong or the native-live downbeat derivation upstream is wrong; regenerate this seed (and its source fixture) with correctly cycling `beatInBar` values, otherwise the simulator's bar behaviour is not representative.

Several beats carry non-integer floating-point artifacts (e.g. `index: 33 → 16120.000000000002`, `index: 67 → 32310.000000000004`, `index: 136 → 65168.00000000001`). Consumers do strict-value timing math on this field — `packages/storage/src/validation.ts` asserts monotonicity with `cur.sourceTimeMs > prev.sourceTimeMs`, and `packages/contracts/src/index.ts` interpolates with it. The artifacts happen not to break the strict-greater check here, but such values make timing/fixture assertions brittle and can cause flaky drift in any test that compares against rounded/expected millisecond values. Prefer clean integer (or consistently rounded) `sourceTimeMs` values in seed/fixture data.

The provenance comment claims this module holds the "exact bytes" of the two fixture files, but the constants below are minified JSON while the referenced fixtures are stored pretty-printed (values are equivalent, byte representation is not). The stated regeneration procedure ("re-copying those two files") would therefore not reproduce these bytes and would turn each constant into a multi-line literal. Please correct the comment to say the values are copied, or record the exact minification step so future regeneration stays reproducible.

apps/desktop/src/features/setup/rkbx-set.content: These assertions do not actually prove the receiving state was rendered. `toContain("receiving")` matches the step id `receiving` that `StepRow` always emits (follow.ts pushes the `receiving` step for every report, rendered as `receiving:`), and `toContain("sudo")` matches the statically imported `RKBX_SUDO_COPY` that is rendered unconditionally. Both would still pass if the panel rendered `no-packets` or `unsupported-version` instead. Assert on the state-specific copy instead, e.g. `toContain("State: receiving")` and `toContain("Receiving packets. No further setup needed.")`, and drop the `sudo` assertion or move it to a check that the remedy is absent.

This test never renders `SetupView`/`RkbxSetupPanel`; it only inspects the `STEP_LABELS` constants. The behavior named in the test title — the controller's self-route button being suppressed — lives in the render guard `!ready && meta.route !== "setup"` in setup-view.tsx and is not exercised here, so that guard could regress while this test stays green. Render the view (or the step list) and assert the `controller` button is absent for a not-ready state, and that `dj`/`library`/`lights` produce the expected routed buttons.

`re-sign` also appears in the always-rendered `RKBX_RESIGN_COPY`/`RKBX_SUDO_COPY` strings, so this assertion passes even if the unsupported-version remedy is dropped or wrong. The test name also promises the "specific missing step", but nothing asserts it. Assert the version-specific remedy text (e.g. `toContain("is not a version rkbx_link supports here")`) and the failing step, e.g. `toContain('aria-label="version missing"')`.

The URL is hardcoded here even though `RKBX_LINK_PROJECT_URL` is the canonical source in `@autolight/rekordbox-live/setup-assistant` (already re-exported/imported by the component). Duplicating the literal means a legitimate URL change breaks the test while a wrong URL in the component could still match. Import `RKBX_LINK_PROJECT_URL` and assert against it; the author-time "curled 200" note is not validated by the test and should not stand in for a link check.

The no-packets snapshot sets `lastAddress: null`, but the only assertion checks the state string; it never verifies the missing-address fallback (`snapshot.packets.lastAddress ?? "none"` in the panel). A regression that rendered `null`/`undefined` or the wrong placeholder would still pass. Assert the rendered fallback, e.g. `toContain("last none")`, alongside `no-packets`.

The `UNAVAILABLE_ON_THIS_DEVICE` branch is driven by prefix matching against `RKBX_MACOS_VERSIONS` (`7.2.8`/`7.2.17`/`7.2.18`), but only the build-tag sample `7.2.10.0333` is covered. There is no boundary coverage (e.g. `7.2.17` supported, `7.2.19` unsupported, whitespace-padded input), so an off-by-one or format change in the version gate would go unnoticed. Add cases around the threshold.

packages/cloud/src/client.test.ts.content: The disabled gate is only proven with `cloudAllowed:false` (both the default-off client at line 129 and this `enabled:true, cloudAllowed:false` case). An implementation that ignores `enabled` entirely and checks only `cloudAllowed` would satisfy all three existing cases, contradicting the test title "unless both ... hold". Add an `enabled:false, cloudAllowed:true` case to actually prove both flags are required.

Only the `lamp` device key is ever used, so a client with a single global minute counter (instead of a per-device one) would still pass this test. Add a call with a distinct device key to assert that device budgets are isolated.

The test title says "takes the first known key", but only `zoneCount` is supplied, so the key precedence (`segments` > `segmentCount` > `zoneCount`) is never actually asserted — a reversed or unordered lookup would still pass. Supply multiple keys and assert the first known one wins.

The show-tick guard is only exercised through `listDevices`. `listScenes` also routes through `guard(...)`; a regression that dropped `ensureNotShowTick` there would go unnoticed. Add a `listScenes` case (and, ideally, assert a normal non-tick call still succeeds).

packages/govee/src/firmware.test.ts.content: This test only covers the `known && segmentedVerified === true` path. The distinct branch in `firmware.ts` for known firmware with an *unverified* channel (`known && !segmentedVerified`, lines 58–62, which returns `"verified-fallback"` with the warning "segmented channel not verified on this unit") is never exercised, so a regression on that path (e.g. accidentally returning `"segmented"`) would go undetected. Add a case such as `policy.decide("1.02.03", "1.02.03", false)` asserting `gate === "verified-fallback"` and that non-null warning.

The warning for the unreadable/unmeasured branch is only asserted with `not.toBeNull()`, so the actual message content is unverified — a wrong, truncated, or misleading warning would still pass. Assert on a distinguishing substring (e.g. `toContain("unreadable")`) so message regressions are caught. Note also that this combination (`saved = "1.02.03"`, `current = "unmeasured"`) is the only one exercising the `segmentedVerified === true` direction here.

This asserts only the `empty string + segmentedVerified === false` combination. The other two combinations of the unmeasured branch's ternary are untested: `decide("1.02.03", "", true)` should yield `"segmented"`, and `decide("1.02.03", "unmeasured", false)` should yield `"verified-fallback"`. Without them, a swap/inversion of the `segmentedVerified ? ... : ...` mapping in `firmware.ts` lines 44–50 would not be caught. The warning content is again only checked for non-nullness.

The jump from `now = 0` to `now = 2000` skips the window boundary entirely, so an off-by-one in the eviction condition (`now - rearmAt[0] >= windowMs` in `firmware.ts`) would not be detected. Add assertions at exactly `now = 999` (fourth `mayRearm()` still `false`) and `now = 1000` (slides and returns `true`). Also assert `rearmCount()` after the slide (should be `1`, the just-pushed re-arm) to lock the reset semantics, since the comment claims the window slides.
